overview.body:
**Ekkeko** ​(*ekkeko*) ‌— ‌Luck, Abundance ​· ​The ​dwarf ​— ​belongs to ‌the ​Incan ​tradition, ‌where ​it is ‌catalogued ​under ‌the ​domain ​"Luck, Abundance". ​The ​name ​means ‌"The ​dwarf".

**Ekkeko** ‌is ​luck, ‌abundance. ​The ‌name means ​"The ‌dwarf" ​and ​belongs ‌to ‌the incan ‌tradition.

​PuniCodex ​restores ‌the ​name as ​**Ekkeko** ‌and ​serves ​its ‌temple at ​[its ‌temple](https://punicodex.com/ekkeko/). ​The ​restoration ​needs no ​distinctive ‌letters ‌or ​diacritics ‌its ASCII ​form ​would ‌lose, ‌which ‌places ‌the name ​in ‌Tier ​2. ​The ​plain ASCII ‌form ​*ekkeko* ​survives ​as ‌a modern ​convenience ​imposed ​by ‌the ​early domain-name ‌system; ​the ‌restoration, ​not ‌the fallback, ‌is ​the ​form ​the ​project defends ‌as ‌philologically ​complete.

the-name.body:
No ​indigenous written ‌attestation ‌survives for ​this ​name; ​**Ekkeko** is ​a ​scholarly transliteration ‌of ​the reconstructed ​spoken ‌form. ​Etymologically the ‌name ​means "The ‌dwarf".

​The ASCII ​form ​*ekkeko* ​survives only ​because ‌the early ​domain-name ‌system could ​not ‌carry ​diacritics; it ‌is ​a technological ‌compromise, ​not an ​ancient ‌spelling. ‌The Unicode ‌restoration ​**Ekkeko** recovers ​the ‌full diacritic ​detail ​of ‌the scholarly ​transliteration ​directly in ‌the ​address bar. ‌The ​restoration needs ​no ​distinctive ​letters or ‌diacritics ‌its ASCII ​form ‌would lose, ​which ​places ‌the name ‌in ‌Tier 2.

‌The ​letter-by-letter transformation ‌runs:

​- ​**e** → ​**E** ‌— Same, ​capitalized
​- **k** ​→ ‌**k** ​— Same
​- ​**k** → ‌**k** ​— Same
‌- ​**e** ‌→ **e** ​— ‌Same
- ‌**k** ​→ **k** ​— ​Same
​- **o** ‌→ ‌**o** — ​Same

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is ​**/ekkeko/** — ​Restored ​scholarly ‌form.

​Phoneme by ​phoneme:

‌- ​**ekkeko** ‌— ​The canonical ‌restored ​form ​Ekkeko.

​For the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the ​closest approximation ‌is: ​Say ‌"ekkeko" ​with the ‌stress ​and ‌length ​implied by ​the ‌scholarly ‌restoration ‌"Ekkeko".

​The ASCII ​form ‌"ekkeko" ​is ​a DNS ‌compromise; ​the ​restoration ‌"Ekkeko" preserves ​the ‌name's ​scholarly ​dignity.

The ​pronunciation ​given ‌above ‌reconstructs the ​sound ‌world ​in ​which ‌Ekkeko was ‌invoked. ‌Modern ‌speakers ​should not ‌expect ​exact ​identity ​with ancient ‌phonology; ​the ​reconstruction ​is a ‌scholarly ​compass, ​not ​a performance ‌prescription. ​The ‌restoration ​Ekkeko ‌keeps the ​prosodic ‌information ‌visible ​even when ​the ​name ​is ‌typed in ‌plain ​ASCII.

​### ‌Sacred ​Name

‌The ​restoration Ekkeko ​returns ​the ​figure ​to ‌scholarly ​recognition.

‌### Luck

​Central ‌domain: ​luck, ‌abundance.

​### ‌Living Tradition

​Honored ​in ‌incan ‌myth, ‌cult, ​and ​cultural memory.

‌### ​Unicode ​Restoration

‌Preserved ​as ​a ‌flagship temple ​despite ‌the ​unregistrable ​plain-ASCII ​form.

​The ‌domain of ‌luck ​is ‌not ​a ​modern ‌abstraction; ‌it names ‌the ‌sphere ​of ‌influence ​that ​ancient worshippers ​attributed ‌to ​Ekkeko. ​Temples, ​texts, ‌and ​iconography converge ​on ​this ‌sphere, ​even ‌when ​local ‌manifestations differ. ​The ‌PuniCodex ‌restoration ​Ekkeko ​restores ​the ​name that ‌governs ‌the ​domain.

mythology.body:
The ​stories of ‌Ekkeko ‌place ​luck, abundance ​at ​the ​center of ​a ‌living ​mythological world.

​### ‌Origins (Myth)

​Ekkeko ‌appears ​in incan ‌tradition ​as ​luck, abundance. ​The ​name's ​meaning, "The ‌dwarf", ​shapes the ‌narratives ​told ‌about this ​figure.

‌### ​Worship and ‌Memory ​(Cult)

​Devotees and ‌later ‌tradition-keepers preserved ‌Ekkeko ​in ​ritual, text, ‌and ​iconography, ​ensuring the ‌name ​survived ​into the ‌modern ​scholarly record.

‌The ​myths ​of Ekkeko ​survive ​in ‌fragments, summaries, ‌and ​later ‌retellings. Each ​version ​reflects the ‌interests ‌of ‌its tellers ‌— ​poets, ‌priests, philosophers, ​and ​scholars. ​The PuniCodex ‌entry ​does not ​privilege ​a ‌single version; ​it ​gathers ​the attestations ‌so ​that ‌readers can ​compare ‌them. The ​restoration ‌Ekkeko ‌gives the ​figure ​a ​stable name ​around ‌which ‌these variants ​orbit.

archaeology.body:
No ​monument, ‌inscription, ‌or ​artifact in ​the ​current ​PuniCodex ​corpus ‌is ​yet ​assigned to ‌Ekkeko ​with ‌certainty. ​That ‌absence ​should ​be read ​honestly: ​for ​a ‌Incan ​name ‌of ​this ‌type the ​material ‌record ​is ‌expected ​to ​be ‌thin, and ‌the ‌primary ​evidence ​remains ‌the ​textual ​testimony gathered ‌in ​the ​Scholarly ‌Sources ​section.

‌Were ​such ​evidence to ​surface, ​it ‌would ‌take ​recognizable ‌forms: ​votive or ​dedicatory ‌inscriptions ‌naming ‌Ekkeko, ‌sanctuary ​or ‌cult remains ​tied ​to ​luck ‌and ​iconography ​matching ​its ‌traditional attributes ​(name ​and ​domain). ‌Each ​candidate ‌would ​be weighed ‌against ​the ‌reconstructed ‌form ​of ​the ​name before ​entering ‌the ‌scholarly ​record.

meditation.body:
To ​contemplate ‌Ekkeko ‌is to ​hold ​the ​idea ​of ​luck, Abundance ‌in ​the ​mind ‌and ​to ask ‌what ​of ‌it ​endures. ​The name ​means ​"The ​dwarf" ‌— ​and a ‌name ​that ‌carries ​its ‌meaning so ​openly ‌invites ​meditation ​rather ‌than ‌mere recollection. ‌The ​tradition ​remembers ‌the ​name as ​luck, ‌Abundance ​· ​The ‌dwarf.

Sit ​with ‌the ​restored ​form ​— Ekkeko ​— ‌and ‌the ​diacritics ‌themselves become ​the ​practice: ‌each ‌mark ‌is ‌a small ​act ‌of ​attention, ​a ​refusal to ‌let ​the ​plain ​ASCII ‌form *ekkeko* ​stand ​in ​for ‌the ​whole. What ‌the ​tradition ‌preserved ​in ‌this name, ‌the ​restoration ​asks ​the ​reader to ‌preserve ‌in ​turn.
